newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven's Stokes threatens to sell - paper.
newsitem.headline: Seven's Stokes threatens to sell - paper.

text.p: The chairman and controlling shareholder of Seven Network Ltd, Kerry Stokes, has threatened to sell his 24.9 percent stake in the television broadcaster if the government changes foreign ownership rules as well as cross-media rules, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said.

Stokes said he would review his position in Seven if the government changed foreign ownership rules in a way that allowed News Corp Ltd to lift its Seven holding to 25 percent from its current 15 percent, the newspaper said.
"Frankly, if those sorts of levels are introduced I would review my own position," Stokes was quoted as saying.

The newspaper said it had learned that the government was considering allowing single foreign investors to take a 25 percent stake in television stations and allowing up to 35 percent for two or more owners.

Foreign ownerships of newspaper would be set at the same level, allowing the government to argue that it had achieved consistency for newspaper, free-to-air television and pay television, the newspaper said.

"If the government is determined to have the media carved up between News and PBL (Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd ), there is no place for me or anbody else," Stokes was quoted as saying.
"If I sell out of Seven, who controls Seven? The government will achieve its objective," he said.
Seven's shares closed up two cents at A$5.70 on Wednesday, having risen 24 percent since late April on speculation News may be allowed to increase its stake.
